title: Mozzarella, Tomato and Basil with Oil and Vinegar Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: A fresh salad of mozzarella cheese, ripe tomatoes and fragrant basil, dressed with extra‑virgin olive oil and wine vinegar. The ingredients are simple, yet together they create a bright, summery flavor typical of Italian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional mozzarella is made from water buffalo milk, but most commercial versions are cow‑milk based.
Basil is considered a symbol of love and happiness in Italy and is often used in wedding dishes.
Tomatoes, native to South America, only became a staple of Mediterranean cooking in the 16th century.
Cold‑pressed extra‑virgin olive oil retains most of the polyphenols that are beneficial for heart health.
Wine vinegar adds a gentle tang and helps improve iron absorption from tomatoes.

items.title: Rich source of calcium
items.content: Mozzarella provides a notable amount of calcium, which supports bone and dental health.

items.title: Antioxidants from tomatoes
items.content: Lycopene, abundant in tomatoes, has strong antioxidant properties and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil supplies monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Vitamins K and B group
items.content: Basil and tomatoes contribute vitamin K as well as B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar stimulates gastric juice production, aiding the digestion of the meal.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People sensitive to milk proteins or lactose may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium content in ready‑made dressing
items.content: If using a pre‑made sauce, watch the salt level, especially for hypertension.

items.title: Acidity of vinegar
items.content: Excessive vinegar intake can irritate the stomach lining in individuals with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish or as a side to pasta, fish or meat. Add arugula, toasted nuts or croutons for extra texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days. Store mozzarella in its brine and keep tomatoes separate to prevent excess moisture.
